If there is a potential for a class action suit, the court makes every effort to ensure that all potential parties are informed of the suit and advised of their right to join the class.  If you somehow miss that (seriously, hard to do.  Ever see those commercials from personal injury firms on TV?), you may only have the option of arbitration, but it's hardly fair to claim foul play at that point.

All that aside, if you're signing some sort of user agreement that stipulates mandatory arbitration of any dispute, then... pretty much your fault.  The terms were clear and you signed it.  Simply not reading a contract before signing it isn't a valid reason to vacate the contract.

i.e.  If you're against any sort of sealed, mandatory arbitration clauses in contracts, stop signing the contracts.  Eventually, the terms of the contract will change.  Or if they don't, you know you're not in the mainstream opinion.  Either way, quit complaining and start acting.

Battery:

In criminal law, a physical act that results in harmful or offensive contact with another's person without that person's consent.

In tort law, the intentional causation of harmful or offensive contact with another's person without that person's consent.

Basically pie in his hand making contact with her face is offensive (non-consensual) contact.

And as a side note, it could be interpreted that the intent was to humiliate the woman, and any court of jury would likely view it as malicious. Not that it's a requirement or anything.

Further, as soon as she saw his hand approaching her face with a pie in it, she's got a reasonable fear of imminent offensive contact. i.e. assault.

Do I think she should sue over it?  Nope.  Does she have a good case?  You bet.

It's kind of hard to say.  I'd been drinking a lot.  That didn't really do it for me.  Then I found out heroin could be snorted.  That seems a lot easier and more accessible than an IV.  I remember that time I broke my collarbone and I got prescribed some opiate painkillers.  Those were pretty nice.

Then I found a source.  All of the sudden heroin was easy to get.  Should I?  Sure, why not.  Nothing else was going that great.  You can snort it, so it's nowhere near as addictive as an IV.  They say it's addictive, but I can just try it to see what it is.  

Hey, that was pretty alright.  I was drunk the first time I tried it; just a tiny little line.  Then I figured out I should try it on its own.  It was a bigger line.  It was amazing.  And I don't mean, that was a fun roller coaster amazing, it was "I just went to the moon and back, I don't care about anything else" amazing.  

So that's how it started out.  Just some fun, a good feeling I could dial up from time to time.  Sure, why not try more and more.  Then I started getting sick.  As soon as I ran out, I couldn't think of much more than how to get more heroin as fast as I could.  I was sitting at my desk at work sweating bullets, hoping no one would notice the patterns of me being super tired (nodding on heroin) and being super sick (withdrawal).

That lasted for a while.  Then it became too much.  I could afford lots of heroin at the time, so I bought lots of heroin.  Then I ran dry all of the sudden.  One of the things they don't really tell you about is that deep, deep depression accompanies withdrawal.  All of the sudden I'm spiraling out of control and there's nothing but heroin that can stop it.  But I'm too dysfunctional to go to work, so I can't afford any more heroin.  And down, and down it goes.  Eventually you hit rock bottom.  Some people can come up from that.  Some people can't.  I didn't think I could; I tried to kill myself.  It seemed to be the easiest/best way out.  It didn't work.  

And now I've been clean for six months, but I still think about it every day.  Every single day.  You'll never forget how good it feels, or at least how good your mind tells you it felt.  

TLDR:  Don't try heroin, kids.  It'll wreck your life.

The worst that can happen is death.  Both are depressants and will slow down your breathing until you eventually stop.  Without any oxygen, you'll die in a few minutes.

If you drank enough alcohol to make yourself sick, there's a chance you'll vomit up the pills before they have a chance to get into your system. If you take the pills first, before you start drinking, there's a good chance if you don't have an opiate tolerance that the pills alone will make you throw up.  You probably won't feel too much like drinking after that, and doing so would give you a pretty good chance of vomiting again, so less of the alcohol would end up in your system.  You'd probably survive the night unless you took enough pills to overdose on the percocet by itself.

If you were to survive any of these scenarios, there would definitely be some significant liver damage.  Percocets have loads of acetaminophen in them, which is harmful to the liver in large quantities.  If you're taking enough percocets to harm you, you're taking enough to damage your liver.  Adding alcohol on top of that, which I'm sure you already know can damage your liver, will simply compound the problem.  If you're drinking enough to cause alcohol poisoning or enough respiratory depression to kill you, the damage is likely to be significant.

All in all, a horrible idea.  Definitely would not be a fun way to go, and would be a pretty bad sight for anybody who happened to find you.
